clue.text: Right scoundrel follows copper, arrested by one

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it in the line of letters
someone arrested is held fast by the police, so one piece is gripped inside another

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A police officer nabs a villain, with the bobby himself being nabbed in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal. The dog breed CUR hides inside ACCURATE, part of the 22 Across theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Right in the sense of correct or exact matches a precise, error-free result.

clue.text: Travelling in America over less important route

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing over another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for America
British roads are graded A (main) and B (minor), so the lesser one carries the letter B

explanation.surface: A tourist driving through the United States takes a quieter back road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, roads are graded A (main) and B (secondary), so a B road is the less important route.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is abroad is away in a foreign country, typically on a trip, so travelling.

clue.text: Drug squad’s first head has major item for PC

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
opening letter of the word
a cape is a headland jutting into the sea
key as an adjective means major or crucial

explanation.surface: The leader of the drug squad has a hot tip for the local police constable.
explanation.walkthrough: PC reads as police constable beside 'drug squad', but it is a personal computer. PEKE (Pekingese) hides in ESCAPE KEY for the 22 Across theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The escape key is a button on a computer keyboard, so a component of a personal computer.

clue.text: Footballers succeeded in stadium close to capital

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside its letters
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: s. is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
an arena is a sports stadium
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A football team wins at a ground near the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, so the surface is nearly literal; s. for succeeded is a genealogy convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous Premier League club, so its players are a team of footballers.

clue.text: What runners do, going straight

blocks.note: first meaning: a two-word British slang phrase for running off fast
second meaning: honest and legal, as a reformed criminal is

explanation.surface: Sprinters head down the track in a straight line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going straight' sounds like running in a line, but it is criminal slang for living lawfully. To leg it is British slang for to run off.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is informal for legitimate, and a former criminal going straight now lives within the law.

clue.text: Quickly do some work with a meat cleaver?

definitions.text: do some work with a meat cleaver

blocks.note: first meaning: an informal exhortation to hurry up

blocks.clueFragment: do some work with a meat cleaver
blocks.note: second meaning: hack, hack again, as a butcher does

explanation.surface: A butcher is told to hurry up and get cleaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a cleaver is used to chop, twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal interjection urging someone to hurry, so it means fast.

clue.text: Maybe Eisenhower‘s daughter dated human being

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
wight is an archaic word for a person

explanation.surface: The President's daughter went out on a date with an ordinary person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' seems to be a verb about romance, but it marks the word that follows as old-fashioned. 'Maybe' signals the answer is one example of a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight was President Eisenhower's first name, one of several names that could be his.

clue.text: Small vehicle, one not supposed to be working

definitions.text: one not supposed to be working

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A little car has broken down and is not meant to be running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' suggests a machine in order; it is a person at work during a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a strikebreaker, who works when fellow union members have walked out.

clue.text: Bird food left on loose stones

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

blocks.note: scree is loose rock on a mountainside
chow is slang for food
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Birdseed has been scattered over a rocky slope.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOW is also a dog breed (the chow chow), guarded inside the answer, as 22 Across explains.
explanation.definitionFit: The screech owl is a small owl species named for its call, so a bird.

clue.text: Gold bar packaging to protect against loss

indicators.note: packaging wraps around its contents, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
save means except, as in 'all save one'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gold ingots are being wrapped up to guard them against theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a gold ingot but means except. TOSA, a Japanese fighting dog, hides inside for the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To autosave is for software to store work automatically so that nothing is lost in a crash.

clue.text: Challenge representative after one shot gun

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it in the line of letters
something shot is wrecked or ruined, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician is challenged to a duel after one shot from a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot gun' reads as one weapon, but 'shot' is the signal to rearrange. PUG is guarded inside, for the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim or motive is to call it into question, dispute or attack it.

clue.text: Go off in southern land — rider may bring this along

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside its letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
an egg that addles goes rotten
to land a catch or prize is to bag it

explanation.surface: A traveller sets out across a southern country on horseback with luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a country; it is the verb, as when an angler lands a fish. 'Go off' is said of eggs turning rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddlebag hangs from a horse's or bicycle's saddle, carrying the rider's belongings.

clue.text: Half hour absorbed by request to keep reading still

indicators.note: something absorbed is soaked up and held inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: PTO, please turn over, asks the reader to continue on the next page
the first two of the word's four letters

explanation.surface: Someone spends half an hour being urged to keep on reading quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning 'even now', but it is a noun: a single frame from a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a photograph, especially a single picture taken from a movie.

clue.text: Large group‘s sorrowful feeling crossing large river

indicators.note: to cross something can mean to span it, so one piece stretches across and around another

blocks.note: pity is sorrow felt for another's suffering
L is the abbreviation for large, and the Ural is a long river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A big crowd feels sad as it fords a great river.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'group's' is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plurality is a large number or multitude of people or things.

clue.text: Theatre sign for bailiffs

blocks.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
an omen is a portent or sign

explanation.surface: A notice outside a theatre warns that the debt collectors are coming.
explanation.walkthrough: Repertory or 'rep' theatre is a company performing a changing programme of plays. POM, short for Pomeranian, hides inside for the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Repo men repossess goods when debts go unpaid, the job British bailiffs do.

clue.text: Units showing strength in field or desert so deployed

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Army units prove their strength on the battlefield or in desert warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' and 'deployed' paint a military scene, but the field is magnetic and 'or' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The oersted is the CGS unit of magnetic field strength, so oersteds measure it.

clue.text: Revolutionary caste’s middle class members making errors

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, which alone is kept
a revolution turns something right round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the central letter of the five
pupils are the members of a school class

explanation.surface: A revolutionary sneers that the middle classes keep getting things wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle class' reads as a social group, but 'middle' belongs to caste and 'class' to its members. PUP hides inside for the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip-ups are minor mistakes or blunders, the same as small errors.

clue.text: Plaits I twisted around girl’s head?

definitions.text: Plaits I twisted around girl’s head?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept
twisting distorts the shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone braids hair and coils it round a girl's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read plainly, it describes what the answer is, plaited hair twisted round a girl's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigtails are braids or bunches of hair worn hanging at the sides or back, often by girls.

clue.text: Turning up as well, fool consumes starter of beef Wellington

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the letters so they read from bottom to top
the starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept
to consume is to take in, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: too means also or as well
a mug is a gullible person, a fool
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fool turns up and wolfs down a beef Wellington starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef Wellington' is a dish, but Wellington here is the rubber boot, named after the Duke.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumboot is a rubber boot, the same thing the British call a wellington or welly.

clue.text: Blunt VIP meeting king

indicators.note: two things meeting are set side by side, one straight after the other

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity, a very important person
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A celebrity speaks frankly when introduced to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' looks like a description of the VIP's manner, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark means plain, bare and unvarnished, as a stark warning is blunt and direct.

clue.text: Instrument in Cats

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat, so two of them make cats

explanation.surface: A musician plays in the orchestra pit of the musical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats suggests the Lloyd Webber show, but it is just a plural: one tom plus another.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a tall, narrow drum played with the hands or sticks, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: What 9, 10, 11, 15, 17, 25, 26, 27 Across and 1, 3 Down do for means of defence

blocks.note: first meaning: each listed answer holds a breed of dog inside it, so keeps it safe
second meaning: animals kept to protect property

explanation.walkthrough: The listed entries hold CHOW, TOSA, PUG, POM, PUP, MUTT, LAB, DINGO, CUR and PEKE; each word is seen as surrounding, or guarding, a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Guard dogs are kept to deter intruders, protecting homes and premises as a form of security.

clue.text: Rubbish couple of teachers from down under

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards runs the letters backwards

blocks.note: Sir is how pupils address a male teacher, and BEd is a teaching degree

explanation.surface: Two Australian teachers are dismissed as useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' suggests Australia; in a down clue it means read from the bottom. A BEd is a Bachelor of Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or remains, which is rubbish in the sense of litter.

clue.text: Not upright, one way or another?

definitions.text: Not upright, one way or another?

blocks.note: surface reading: horizontal rather than standing up
setter's reading: also not upright morally, that is telling untruths

explanation.walkthrough: Upright means both vertical and honest; the answer fails on both counts, being flat and also dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying down is horizontal, and someone lying is speaking falsely, so neither stands straight.

clue.text: Black or blue seam unkempt, tatty at the edges

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters stay

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
first and last letters of the word
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A coal seam is black, and a bruised, scruffy miner is ragged around the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black or blue' hints at bruising, but covers two senses: sooty and obscene. MUTT hides inside for the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Smutty means dirtied with soot, which is black, and also indecent, which blue describes.

clue.text: Twice bail criminal making a sound when speaking

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: the word written out two times

explanation.surface: A crook released on bail for a second time speaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' doubles the fodder before it is rearranged. LAB, for Labrador, hides inside for the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilabial is a consonant such as p, b or m, articulated with both lips together.

clue.text: Husband, getting on during illness, is resisting

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
someone getting on in years is old
in means during, as in 'in the night'
gout is a painful joint condition

explanation.surface: An ageing husband stays stubborn while unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like a container signal, but here it simply gives IN. DINGO, the Australian wild dog, hides inside for the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding out means refusing to give in or yield, standing firm against pressure.

clue.text: Scotswoman, half-cut one from Jura, perhaps

indicators.note: cutting something in half removes half of it, so the back half of the word is lost

blocks.note: Jura is a Scottish island, so someone living there is an islander

explanation.surface: A Scottish woman is drunk on Jura whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy, and Jura is also a whisky, but here it means cut in half. Jura is an island in the Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Isla is a popular Scottish girl's name, so a Scotswoman could bear it.
